AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Lainez called the Closed Session meeting to order at 5:06 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any Closed Session items.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The members of the City Council and Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:08 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION The members of the City Council and Successor Agency reconvened to open session at 6:17 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed session Item No. 1, stating that with the entire Council present, the item was discussed. Staff provided a presentation, the Council gave direction, and no final reportable action was taken.

Item No. 2 was discussed, but not concluded.

Item Nos. 3 and 4 were not discussed.

City Attorney Tapia concluded that the Closed Session Item Nos. 2-4 discussions will continue after the regular City Council meeting items.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Lainez called the regular City Council meeting to order at 6:17 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Director of Public Works Abbas led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Altamirano offered the invocation.

PUBLIC COMMENT The City received and saved as part of the record a written public comment regarding Commerce Crush Volleyball.

Assistant Fire Chief Paul Stump from the Los Angeles County Fire Department provided a presentation on programs offered through the department. Mayor Lainez expressed gratitude to Assistant Fire Chief for the information. Councilmember Rebollo will share her questions and comments with the liaison Herlinda Chico after the meeting.

Yvonne Sandoval, president of the Senior Club, shared the club offerings and events for seniors 50 and over at the Senior Center. She expressed her gratitude to the Parks and Recreation Department for supporting senior programming.

Gloria Nezahualcoyotl provided public comment, in Spanish, expressing her gratitude for the Parks and Recreation Department. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Mayor Lainez pulled Consent Calendar Item No. 6 for a separate discussion.

2.. Approval of Minutes Action Taken: Approved the minutes of the Regular City Council meeting of Tuesday, January 27, 2026, held at 6:00 p.m.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Altamirano had no reports.

Councilmember Rebollo expressed her gratitude to the staff of the Parks and Recreation Department for the Employee Services Award Ceremony. She would like to congratulate all the City Staff and retirees that were recognized at the event for their years of service. She also expressed her gratitude to City Staff for their dedication in keeping Commerce the Model City. She expressed her gratitude to Yvonne Sandoval, president of the Senior Club, for her announcements of the offerings of the Senior Center.

Councilmember Argumedo expressed his gratitude to City staff for their contributions to the City after attending the Employee Services Awards Ceremony.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia expressed her gratitude to City Staff for their continued hard work and impact on the City after attending the Employee Services Award Ceremony. She requests that the Parks and Recreation and Library Departments coordinate to provide Homework Help Services to the Veteran's Park Community. She also requested to have the lights around city hall be lit in different colors to reflect certain events such as Veteran's Day and Mental Health Awareness. City Manager Hernandez will follow up with City Staff on those requests.

Mayor Lainez received community member requests for more lights at the Bristow Park parking lot, and informed the community that the City was already addressing this request. He expressed gratitude towards the Veteran's Park community for their patience regarding the projects around the area. He attended the Employee Services Award Ceremony and expressed his gratitude towards the Parks and Recreation Department for organizing the event, to all the employees being recognized, and to Parks & Recreation staff members Anthony and Melissa for their decorations, and Lisa Macias for stepping in last minute as the M.C. 

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION Mayor Lainez recessed to Closed Session at 7:04 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

8.. Adopt Resolution No. 26- of Intention to Amend the City’s CALPERS Contract to Provide Up to Two (2) Years of Additional Service Credit (“Golden Handshake”) and to Receive and Disclose the Actuarial Cost Analysis Pursuant to Government Code Sections 20903 and 7507 and the Introduction of an Ordinance Authorizing an Amendment to the Contract Between the City Council of the City of Commerce, California and the Board of Administration of the California Public Employees’ Retirement System  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo City Manager Hernandez provided a presentation on the item.

3.. Agreement with GMV Syncromatics, Inc. for Intelligent Transportation System Maintenance and Support Action Taken: Adopted Resolution No. 2026-06 approving the Agreement with GMV Syncromatics, Inc. for ITS Maintenance and Support.

4.. Adoption of Resolution No. 2026- Declaring that Weeds, Brush, Rubbish, and Refuse are a Public Nuisance - Weed Abatement Action Taken: Adopted Resolution No. 2026-07 declaring that weeds, brush rubbish and refuse upon or in front of the specified properties in the City are a seasonal and recurrent public nuisance, and declaring its intention to provide for abatement thereof.  

9.. Approval of Professional Services Agreement for the Preparation of Plans, Specifications, and Engineer’s Estimate (PS&E) for a New Pocket Park Located on Gage Avenue and Zindell Avenue  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Public Works Abbas provided a presentation on the item.

City Manager Hernandez provided additional comments that once approved, City Staff will execute the agreement with the Council selected firm and schedule a public hearing for the residents.

Councilmember Rebollo would like to ensure that the Vista Del Rio residents receive updates on this project as well as the Modelo project progress. 


7.. Mural Installation for the Pathways for Hope Project (Clean California Cycle 1 Grant) Project Acceptance  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Public Works Abbas provided a presentation on the item. 

Councilmember Argumedo expressed interest in completing the murals on the other side of the tunnels by the Bandini neighborhood. He would also like to continue upgrading the lights around the murals and Washington.

5.. Authorization to Release the Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Revitalization of Telegraph Rd and Washington Blvd Corridors Project Action Taken: Authorized staff to release the Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Revitalization of Telegraph Road (from city limit to city limit) and Washington Boulevard (from Telegraph Rd to Garfield Ave) Corridors Project.

1.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 11A, 11A-SA, 11B, and 11C Action Taken: Approved the bills and claims set forth in Warrant Registers No. 11A dated February 10, 2026, 11A-SA dated January 22, 2026, 11B for the period of January 22, 2026 through January 26, 2026, and 11C for the period of January 28, 2026 through February 4, 2026. 

6.. Budget Appropriation for the Temporary Recreation Volleyball Structure  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Mayor Lainez pulled Consent Calendar Item No. 6 for a separate discussion.

City Manager Hernandez provided background information on the item. 

Assistant Director of Parks and Recreation Marquez provided a presentation on the item. 

Councilmember Rebollo expressed her gratitude to staff for continuing to provide services to the residents of the Veteran's Park neighborhood.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session Item Nos. 2, 3, and 4, stating that with the entire Council was present, the three items were discussed. Staff provided presentations, the Council gave directions, and no final reportable action was taken on any of the items.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION The members of the City Council and Successor Agency reconvened to open session at 8:38 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT There being no further business before the City Council, Mayor Lainez adjourned the meeting at 8:39 p.m.

SCHEDULED MATTERS
